title: Normalized comparison of principal scalar cones with canonical derived quotients
statement: Let l be prime, let E/Q_l be finite, and let X be any scheme, with the pulled-back integral coefficient ring R and canonical quotient maps of [sk-def-pe-derived-completion]. Let d be an endomorphism of the regular condensed integral module whose section formula is multiplication by the specified uniformizer. Write a_n(M) for its (n+1)-st power acting on an unbounded complex M and suppose a_(n+1)(M)=d_M followed by a_n(M). Then the standard scalar-cone functors Q Cone(a_n) admit natural isomorphisms to canonical derived coefficient extension at level n+1 followed by exact restriction to R. They send the cone transition (d,id) to integralStep and the cone inclusion to the actual derived scalar-extension adjunction unit. There are coherent shifts on the latter derived functors for which these isomorphisms commute with the inverse standard mappingCone.shiftIso at every integer shift. With these shifts the functors are additive and triangulated. All comparisons refer to the existing functors and adjunctions, without changing any coefficient objects.

proof.text: The prescribed scalar formula identifies d with multiplication by the uniformizer. Apply the exact coefficient sequence in det-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution at exponent n+1. Its two-term free complex augments to the quotient in degree zero and is K-flat by bounded-flat K-flatness. This is a genuine principal resolution, without requiring the scalar to act injectively on the input complex.

proof.text: Choose a flat-term K-flat resolution of each input complex. Signed total-tensor interchange identifies tensoring the two-term coefficient resolution with the scalar mapping cone. The tensor augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism. Balanced tensor generators identify the restricted ordinary extension of scalars with tensor by the quotient coefficient. The universal derived computation counit and the resolving-category localization extend this comparison naturally to every unbounded complex and every derived morphism.

proof.text: The coefficient quotient transition is lifted by multiplication by d in degree -1 and the identity in degree zero. The supplied scalar-power equality is precisely its chain-map equation. Naturality of the tensor augmentation identifies the resulting mapping-cone map with the canonical integralStep defined by composition of the actual scalar-extension adjunctions. The degree-zero cone inclusion is the ordinary coefficient-extension unit; its normalized derived comparison is therefore the actual derived adjunction unit.

proof.text: The tensor shift map on the two-term resolution has formula (x,y) to (x,(-1)^r y), which is the inverse of mappingCone.shiftIso. It commutes with all comparison maps. Localize this coherent shift comparison to define sF, obtaining the displayed shift equation. Tensoring is additive and carries cone triangles to cone triangles, including their boundary after this signed shift, hence the descended functor is triangulated. Zero complexes, negative shifts and the empty scheme satisfy the same formulas.

theorem derived_principal_normalization
    (d : End (Mod.regular (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E)))
    (hd : ∀ (S : Profinite.{u}ᵒᵖ) (a : (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E).obj.obj S)
      (s : S.unop), ((d.hom.hom.app S) a).down s =
        Padic.coefficientExtensionUniformizer l E * a.down s)
    (hs : ∀ (n : ℕ) (M : CochainComplex (AdicCompletion.Modules l E X) ℤ),
      DerivedNakayama.scalarOnComplex l E X (d ^ (n + 1 + 1)) M =
        DerivedNakayama.scalarOnComplex l E X d M ≫
          DerivedNakayama.scalarOnComplex l E X (d ^ (n + 1)) M) :
    ∃ (sF : ∀ n : ℕ, (reduction l E X n).CommShift ℤ)
      (κ : ∀ n : ℕ, DerivedNakayama.coneFunctor l E X (d ^ (n + 1)) ≅
        DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ reduction l E X n),
      (∀ n : ℕ, (reduction l E X n).Additive ∧
        @Functor.IsTriangulated _ _ _ _ _ _ (reduction l E X n)
          (sF n) _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (M : CochainComplex (AdicCompletion.Modules l E X) ℤ),
        DerivedCategory.Q.map (CochainComplex.mappingCone.map
          (DerivedNakayama.scalarOnComplex l E X (d ^ (n + 1 + 1)) M)
          (DerivedNakayama.scalarOnComplex l E X (d ^ (n + 1)) M)
          (DerivedNakayama.scalarOnComplex l E X d M) (𝟙 M)
          ((Category.comp_id _).trans (hs n M))) ≫ (κ n).hom.app M =
            (κ (n + 1)).hom.app M ≫
              AdicCompletion.integralStep l E X (DerivedCategory.Q.obj M) n) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (M : CochainComplex (AdicCompletion.Modules l E X) ℤ),
        DerivedCategory.Q.map (CochainComplex.mappingCone.inr
          (DerivedNakayama.scalarOnComplex l E X (d ^ (n + 1)) M)) ≫
            (κ n).hom.app M =
          (Mod.derivedExtendMapDerivedCategoryAdjunction
            (AdicCompletion.quotient l E X n)).unit.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj M)) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (r : ℤ) (M : CochainComplex (AdicCompletion.Modules l E X) ℤ),
        DerivedCategory.Q.map
            (CochainComplex.mappingCone.shiftIso
              (DerivedNakayama.scalarOnComplex l E X (d ^ (n + 1)) M) r).inv ≫
            (DerivedCategory.Q.commShiftIso r).hom.app
              (CochainComplex.mappingCone
                (DerivedNakayama.scalarOnComplex l E X (d ^ (n + 1)) M)) ≫
            ((κ n).hom.app M)⟦r⟧' =
          (κ n).hom.app (M⟦r⟧) ≫
            (reduction l E X n).map ((DerivedCategory.Q.commShiftIso r).hom.app M) ≫
            (Functor.commShiftIso (self := sF n) (reduction l E X n) r).hom.app
              (DerivedCategory.Q.obj M))
